role_summary: Mini-CTO of Turing's enterprise GenAI practice. Runs the technical side of an applied AI consulting and delivery operation serving Fortune 500 clients with a specific vertical focus on BFSI, especially capital markets and adjacent institutional-finance workflows. The clearest bank-side target is Executive Director at a major bank, with equivalent seniority allowed at tech companies, market-infrastructure firms, and other relevant BFSI organizations. Equally comfortable whiteboarding architecture with engineers and briefing a CIO. Not a research role — applied GenAI delivery at enterprise scale.

minimum_bar.experience_note: Must hit the ground running. 15yr floor is hard — no exceptions.
minimum_bar.title_floor: Executive Director at a major bank, or Director/Senior Director/Head of/Principal Engineer/Architect/VP (context-dependent) at equivalent-scope tech or BFSI organizations
minimum_bar.title_ceiling_note: Major-bank MD, global head, SVP at large org, EVP, CDAO, CXO at large org, CTO at 100+ person engineering org, Partner at Big4 = likely too senior and too expensive. Exception: CTO/CEO at scrappy startup (<150 employees) — apply Jon Dorando principle.
minimum_bar.technical_depth: Must show direct, personal involvement in BUILDING AI systems. Not managing a team that builds, not selling it, not developing product strategy around it.
minimum_bar.bfsi_domain: At least one BFSI employer or BFSI-domain project, with highest priority on capital markets and adjacent institutional-finance workflows: Goldman, Morgan Stanley, Citi, JPMorgan, BofA, BlackRock, Vanguard, Apollo, Tradeweb, Bloomberg, market infrastructure, asset management, investment banking, post-trade, research, credit/risk/trading systems. Payments, mortgage, treasury, and insurance are supportive but lower-priority domains.
minimum_bar.genai_fluency: Post-2022 GenAI work required. Must show evidence of: LLM deployment, RAG system design, agentic architectures, evaluation frameworks, or fine-tuning. GenAI strategy without implementation evidence is insufficient.
minimum_bar.location: Current location must be NYC metro (NYC, NJ, CT commuter zone). Remote or other cities = skip.

archetypes: Spent 10+ years building fixed income/credit trading systems at Tradeweb/Goldman/BofA, then pivoted to leading GenAI strategy at an enterprise AI company
VP ML/Data Science at Goldman building credit scoring and AI analytics, then led R&D at a startup, now leads AI Labs at a major hedge fund
Engineering Director & Head of GenAI at a Tier-1 bank for 10+ years, previously VP at another major bank
CTO at a scrappy fintech startup (<150 employees) personally building agentic AI for institutional finance clients

preview_scan_criteria.rule: Before opening any profile, triage from preview using these four signals. If two or more are failing, skip without opening.
signals: TITLE — At major banks, Executive Director is the cleanest target. Equivalent Director, Senior Director, Head of, Principal, VP, or startup CTO titles can fit outside banking if the scope is right. SVP/MD/EVP/CXO/Partner = skip. IC titles (Senior Engineer, Staff Engineer) = skip unless at a frontier BFSI firm.

COMPANY — Must show BFSI employer (Goldman, JPMorgan, Citi, BofA, Morgan Stanley, BlackRock, Vanguard, Tradeweb, Bloomberg, Freddie Mac, Fannie Mae, TIAA, Prudential, fintech at scale) OR consulting firm serving BFSI (Deloitte, Accenture, McKinsey) OR BFSI-focused startup/fintech.
YEARS — Must show 15+ years visible. If LinkedIn shows <15yr total career, skip.

HEADER KEYWORDS — Look for GenAI/AI builder language in the headline: LLM, RAG, agentic, LangGraph, orchestration, GenAI, applied AI, ML engineering. Red flags that justify skip without opening: Solutions Architect, AI Products, AI Transformation, AI Strategy, Customer Success, Pre-Sales, Product Manager.

hard_skips: Zero BFSI employer or BFSI-domain project in entire career
Pure researcher with no production deployment experience
Annotation/data labeling worker (Scale AI, Outlier, Appen)
IT auditor, QA tester with no ML crossover

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: Solutions Architect at cloud vendor (AWS, Azure, GCP)
clear_skips_from_review.reason: Customer-facing pre-sales/demos, not production AI engineering. Richa Kaul pattern.
clear_skips_from_review.example: Head of Customer Solutions / Sr. Leader Solutions Architecture @ AWS

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: Head of AI Products / VP AI Products
clear_skips_from_review.reason: Product management layer over engineering. Not the hands-on technical depth required. Amir Elkabir pattern.
clear_skips_from_review.example: Executive Director & Head of AI Products @ JPMorgan

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: AI Transformation Executive / AI Strategy Lead
clear_skips_from_review.reason: Strategy and transformation framing without implementation evidence.
clear_skips_from_review.example: Chief AI Transformation Officer, AI Strategy & Innovation Lead

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: CTO at massive org (400+ person engineering org, $100M+ budget)
clear_skips_from_review.reason: Scope and comp ceiling mismatch. Robert Babinski pattern.
clear_skips_from_review.example: CTO Investments & Capital Markets @ Freddie Mac (400-person org)

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: MD / EVP / CDAO / CXO at large financial institution
clear_skips_from_review.reason: Too senior, too expensive. Swatee Singh pattern.
clear_skips_from_review.example: EVP & CDAIO @ TIAA, MD @ Barclays (1,100-person team)

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: AI experience = adopting tools, not building systems
clear_skips_from_review.reason: Implementing GitHub Copilot, Devin, or off-the-shelf AI tools is not the same as building AI systems.
clear_skips_from_review.example: Gerard Pento pattern: implementing GitHub Copilot and Devin across engineering

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: Customer Success or Pre-Sales adjacent role
clear_skips_from_review.reason: Client-facing demos and adoption, not engineering delivery.
clear_skips_from_review.example: Head of Customer Solutions, Pre-Sales Solutions Architect

clear_skips_from_review.reason: Directs engineering, does not build. Shannon Mullen pattern.
clear_skips_from_review.example: SVP Data & Analytics Product Manager @ Citi

clear_skips_from_review.reason: No enterprise-scale AI practice leadership demonstrated.

gate_evaluation_order.name: Diversity (first pass only)
gate_evaluation_order.rule: Women OR non-Indian candidates only on diversity pass. South Asian males = skip without opening.

gate_evaluation_order.name: Seniority calibration
gate_evaluation_order.rule: See title_floor and title_ceiling_note. Major-bank Executive Director is the anchor target. Bank VP is often below scope unless unusually broad. Major-bank MD or global-head profiles are usually above scope. Apply Jon Dorando principle for startup CTOs (<150 employees). Apply Robert Babinski rule for large-org CTOs (400+ person org).

gate_evaluation_order.name: Technical depth (hard filter)
pass_signals: Specific tools personally used: LangGraph, LlamaIndex, DSPy, Haystack, CrewAI, Temporal, etc.
Phrases: I architected, I implemented, I built, I deployed to production
Fine-tuned models, built RAG pipelines, designed evaluation frameworks themselves
ML engineering titles with implementation evidence
fail_signals: Head of AI Products / VP AI Products
CDO with no hands-on engineering evidence
AI experience = GitHub Copilot / Devin adoption

gate_evaluation_order.name: BFSI domain
gate_evaluation_order.rule: At least one BFSI employer or BFSI-domain project. Highest weight goes to capital markets, asset management, investment banking, post-trade, market infrastructure, and adjacent institutional-finance workflows. Payments, mortgage, treasury, and insurance are valid but lower-priority. Not healthcare, retail, or tech-adjacent.

gate_evaluation_order.name: GenAI fluency
gate_evaluation_order.rule: Post-2022 work with evidence of LLM deployment, RAG system design, agentic architectures, evaluation frameworks, RLHF/fine-tuning, or model selection/benchmarking. Strategy without implementation = insufficient.
